transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Desai (Redwood AE), Ethan Moore (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Solutions), Jonah Lee (NeptuneVector Head of Cloud), Marta Ivanova (NeptuneVector Platform), Ravi Singh (NeptuneVector Security), Leah Torres (NeptuneVector DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto): Align on packaging and network/crypto patterns for listing + pilot.

Transcript:
00:00 Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do a quick run through of the marketplace playbook and the LLM gateway patterns, then handoff to the SE bits. um, Ethan is gonna drive the technical details.
00:18 Jonah: Great, thanks. Quick note, we have a hard deadline for the marketplace listing by mid-September, so we want to make sure the packaging and compliance bits are clear.
00:28 Ethan: Got it. I'll start with the high level — two patterns we recommend: a hosted listing model (Redwood hosted with private egress) and a hybrid marketplace connector (customer-managed gateway deployed in VPC). For NeptuneVector, you indicated preference for the hybrid flow, correct?
00:43 Marta: Yeah we prefer hybrid. We need the connector in our VPC so data never leaves our network. Also must integrate with our KMS cluster for model keys.
00:55 Priya: Perfect. On the playbook side we'll provide: helm chart, sample values.yaml, a packaging checklist for marketplace certs, and a reference topology diagram. Link after the call.
01:10 Leah: When you say helm chart — is that an operator or just a helm release? Our infra team prefers operatorless deployments.
01:20 Ethan: It's a plain helm chart (no operator). We also produce a container image that is OCI-compliant and a sidecar for metrics. We'll include an example manifests folder.
01:34 Ravi: Regarding KMS — we need to understand if Redwood requires persistent access to our KMS keys or if we can use a temporary wrapped key exchange. Security and audit are big for us.
01:47 Samir: Good question. For the hybrid gateway the flow is: customer encrypts model tokens with your KMS/HSM and provides wrapped keys to the gateway; Redwood doesn't hold plaintext keys. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via PKCS11. There is an optional short-lived token exchange for provisioning.
02:05 Jonah: Uh, any gotchas on key rotation? We rotate keys every 30 days.
02:10 Ethan: Rotation is supported — the helm chart includes a rotation cronjob example that fetches new wrapped keys, updates the secret store in the pod and restarts the minimal services; we documented zero-downtime rotation patterns. We'll add your rotation cadence to the runbook.
02:28 Speaker 1 (Marta?): Sorry can I ask about VPC networking — do you need peering, private link, or NAT?
02:35 Ethan: We support three connectivity modes: VPC peering (cross-account/VPC), PrivateLink endpoint (recommended for managed listing on AWS), or egress-only NAT with strict whitelist. Each has tradeoffs: PrivateLink gives private connectivity and no public egress; peering is simpler but requires route management.
02:53 Leah: We prefer PrivateLink but our infra has a limited quota for endpoints right now. Could we do peering for pilot then switch to PrivateLink for GA?
03:02 Priya: Absolutely — many customers do peering in pilot then migrate. We'll document the migration steps.
03:12 Jonah: On the marketplace side, what artifacts are required for listing approval?
03:16 Priya: Checklist: helm chart, values.yaml, a deploy/rollback playbook, a security questionnaire (we'll fill 80% but need your SOC2 excerpts), telemetry schema for usage/billing, and sample SLAs. Also an image scan report (snyk/other) and a signed attestation for third-party components.
03:36 Ravi: We'll need to redact some SOC2 items. Is a summarized compliance matrix OK?
03:40 Priya: Yes, summary plus specific evidentiary docs for controls of interest. We'll mark which controls we need for the listing review.
03:48 Ethan: Switching to runtime — we should talk model variants and quantization. For latency-sensitive routes we recommend int8 quant on our runtime; that reduces mem and cost but can impact quality slightly.
04:03 Marta: Can we pin specific model versions per route? We have a mix of user-facing low-latency and offline batch.
04:10 Ethan: You can pin versions and set routing polices (canary, a/b, or fallback to hosted). The runtime supports KV cache sharing for faster prefix reuse.
04:21 Jonah: Cost question — if we run quantized model on-private, how is billing handled? Do we get usage billing from Redwood or is it just internal compute?
04:30 Priya: For hybrid connector listings there's a split: marketplace metering still records usage (for revenue share/listing fees) while compute cost is handled by customer infra. We'll include an example billing report in the package.
04:44 Leah: Telemetry — what does Redwood expect us to emit?
04:49 Samir: Minimal: request_id, model_version, route_id, token_count, latency_ms, and a success/error code. For billing we additionally capture token_count normalized to Redwood's unit. We'll provide a telemetry shim that emits to your Prometheus/OTLP endpoint.
05:05 Ravi: Is telemetry encrypted in flight?
05:08 Ethan: Yes TLS 1.3, mTLS optional for OTLP. We'll include config examples.
05:15 Jonah: A quick thing on canary/rollout: do you support progressive traffic shifting?
05:19 Ethan: Yes, the deployment controller supports traffic splits with weighted routing and automatic rollback on error thresholds. We'll include canary policy examples (50/50 for 24h etc).
05:33 Marta: For the helm chart, do you expect us to publish to your registry?
05:36 Priya: We usually ask partners to publish container images to their own registry and provide manifest references; the marketplace listing then references the images. Optionally we can host a replica in Redwood's registry for convenience during review.
05:51 Jonah: Are there known integration pitfalls? Something you've seen break during certification?
05:55 Ethan: Biggest issues: incorrect CORS on control plane endpoints, missing env var for KMS region, and metrics not matching the expected schema (which blocks billing). We run an automated cert lint that highlights these.
06:12 Leah: On PKI — do we support customer-supplied TLS certs or only auto-generated Let's Encrypt certs?
06:18 Samir: Both. For marketplace you often need customer-supplied certs for private endpoints. We support cert-manager integration or manual secrets.
06:26 Ravi: Audit logs — we need syslog forwarding to our SIEM with PII redaction. Is that supported?
06:31 Ethan: Yes, we can forward audit events to your syslog/OTLP. We also support configurable scrubbing rules in the gateway to redact headers/body fields. We'll share the scrub rules template.
06:47 Priya: I'll pause — any pressing questions before we move to the pilot runbook?
06:51 Jonah: Security: what's the minimum vetting for pilot customers versus GA?
06:55 Priya: Pilot vetting is lighter: short security questionnaire, network allowlist, and shared responsibility doc. GA requires the full marketplace security checklist and image scan results. We'll mark those in the playbook.
07:09 Ethan: Pilot runbook steps (high level): 1) create staging account and VPC, 2) provide list of IPs for whitelisting, 3) install helm chart with sample values, 4) run integration smoke tests (connectivity, telemetry, KMS key unwrap), 5) 48-72h canary with low traffic, 6) review billing events. We'll attach test scripts.
07:35 Marta: Do you have those smoke tests as runnable scripts?
07:38 Ethan: Yes, bash + python scripts and a kube job; we'll drop them in the repo.
07:44 Speaker 2 (Jonah or Samir): Can we also run a perf benchmark locally to validate latency envelope?
07:49 Samir: We'll share a lightweight perf harness — it simulates token distributions and measures p50/p95. It requires GPU access; for pilot we can run on a small instance.
08:00 Leah: GPU access — we don't want to expose our internal GPU fleet. Does Redwood provide a test GPU for benchmarking?
08:07 Priya: Redwood provides a hosted benchmark sandbox (limited credits) if you want to run a quick perf test without touching your infra. For the hybrid connector benchmark you'd run locally; we can help with configs.
08:20 Jonah: About billing metering again — if we run a locally deployed gateway, how is token metering enforced?
08:26 Samir: The gateway emits signed metering events back to Redwood's billing endpoint. Events are signed with a rotating keypair you provision; we verify and ingest for marketplace revenue share. We can operate in 'audit-only' mode during pilot.
08:44 Ravi: Signing keys — is that additional complexity for us?
08:47 Ethan: It's a short-lived keypair per deployment; we provide tooling to rotate and provision. We'll include step-by-step CLI commands.
08:56 Priya: Quick pause — I want to surface one customer's ask: support for quantized model variants that maintain quality — any guidance?
09:04 Ethan: Quantization guidance: do an evaluation on a holdout prompt set; use int8 with per-channel scaling, evaluate p95 degrade. For many LLMs int8 has negligible quality delta on generation tasks but impacts some fine-grained classification. We'll provide recommended quant config files.
09:22 Marta: Do you support dynamic batching in the gateway or is batching only in the Redwood runtime?
09:27 Samir: Gateway does simple request coalescing but heavy batching is in the Redwood runtime. For on-prem we provide a small batching library that can be enabled. There are latency tradeoffs; we'll document expected p50/p95 shifts.
09:44 Jonah: Any legal/procurement frictions we should prep for?
09:48 Priya: Standard NDA + MSA patterns. For marketplace listing there's a revenue share addendum. We'll share sample contract language. Procurement often asks about indemnity — we have a marketplace partner doc that covers that.
09:59 Leah: Okay, next — CI/CD for releases: do you want us to attach a webhook for image updates?
10:04 Ethan: We recommend image tags and digest pinning for reproducible deploys. Webhook can be used for automated review; we'll include a GitHub Actions example.
10:14 Marta: Great. On SSO/SSO integration for the dashboard — we want SAML/SCIM for user provisioning.
10:20 Priya: We'll ship a SAML app template and SCIM provisioning example. Marketplace listing requires a section about RBAC mapping; include that in the playbook.
10:33 Jonah: Okay can we talk about timeline? We have internal release on 2026-09-20 and need marketplace listing approved before that. Is that feasible?
10:41 Priya: Feasible if pilot runs early September and you provide SOC2 excerpts quickly. Our cert review typically takes 7-10 business days once artifacts are complete. So timeline is tight but doable.
10:52 Ethan: Concrete plan: drop artifacts by 2026-09-01, run connectivity tests by 2026-09-05, pilot kick-off 2026-09-08, and certification review 2026-09-15.
11:06 Jonah: Sounds good. A few smaller items — secrets management: do you require Vault specific APIs (HashiCorp) or will AWS Secrets Manager be fine?
11:13 Samir: We support both via abstraction; the helm chart has a secrets provider interface. For Vault we'll include example auth with AppRole.
11:25 Ravi: For audit retention, how long does Redwood keep logs when gateway is hybrid?
11:30 Priya: For hybrid we store minimal metadata for billing for 90 days by default; customer can opt-in to longer retention in the marketplace listing configuration. Full request/response logs remain with the customer unless you opt to forward them to Redwood for troubleshooting.
11:47 Marta: Is there a supported upgrade path for the gateway if we need a breaking change?
11:51 Ethan: We support canary upgrade charts and a migration guide. If it's breaking we recommend a two-stage rollout: compatibility mode (feature flags) followed by traffic migration.
12:05 Leah: Would like to see the runbook now — even a skeleton.
12:08 Priya: I'll post the skeleton right after — it has checkboxes for each required artifact.
12:15 Jonah: Ok quick perf question — what's the expected p95 for a 2k token prompt on a quantized MPT-ish model deployed on an n1-standard with a T4?
12:26 Samir: Hmm that one varies widely; rough ballpark p50 ~ 120ms per token, p95 ~ 600-900ms per token depending on batching and kernel selection — we'll give you a more accurate table for the model family you plan to use.
12:46 Ethan: We'll run a small benchmark and post numbers in the repo.
12:50 Speaker 3 (Marta): Any notes on support SLAs for pilot?
12:54 Priya: Pilot support is standard business-hours with a named AE/SE. For Dedicated or Enterprise lists we provide 24x7 on-call and SLA credits.
13:05 Jonah: Great. I think that's covered. Shall we go through specific next steps?
13:10 Priya: Yes. Recap: 1) Priya to share marketplace packaging checklist + helm chart link by 2026-09-01; 2) Ethan + Marta run connectivity/VPC/KMS tests by 2026-09-05; 3) NeptuneVector (Ravi) to upload compliance matrix by 2026-09-10; 4) Pilot kickoff 2026-09-08 (invite will be sent). Also we'll share perf harness and smoke tests.
13:36 Jonah: One more — is there a credential rotation policy we need to follow in the pilot runbook?
13:41 Ethan: We'll include recommended rotation intervals and automated scripts.
13:45 Priya: Ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and invites.
13:50 Leah: Thanks, bye.
13:52 Ethan: Thanks all, bye.
